links.outcome: Error rates (incorrectly filled fields) with versus without selective human review of low-confidence fields
links.effect: Hybrid review lowered IFF: medium forms Auto with annotations 5% vs Hybrid with annotations 1%; large forms 7% vs 5%. Hybrid without annotations: 10% to 3% in medium forms.
links.quote: The hybrid configuration consistently improves suggestion correctness, while the most substantial error mitigation is observed in the Incorrectly Filled Fields Percentage, which declines markedly–from 10% to 3% in medium forms and by 5 percentage points in large forms.

links.outcome: Speech recognition error rates in Persian code-switched clinical speech
links.effect: Whisper WER 18.4% on standard Persian clinical speech, rising to 28.7% with heavy code-switching; Google Speech-to-Text WER 32.1%. Language-stratified performance was reported for code-switched segments.
links.quote: On the evaluation dataset, the Whisper model achieved a Word Error Rate (WER) of 18.4% on standard Persian clinical speech, increasing to 28.7% in segments exhibiting heavy code-switching.

links.outcome: Scribe-like transcript errors including hallucinated, unsupported, or mismapped content in structured entries
links.effect: Errors by stage: ASR and code-switching 42%, refinement 18% (LLM over-correcting or adding unsupported modifiers), mapping 40%. Residual error rates of about 5-10% persist in complex forms.
links.quote: Refinement Errors (18%): These instances involved the LLM over-correcting telegraphic dictation or introducing unsupported modifiers, which occasionally altered the original clinical nuance without changing core facts.

links.outcome: ASR accuracy on code-switched and informal non-English clinical dictation
links.effect: Whisper WER increased from 18.4% to 28.7% in heavily code-switched segments. ASR-only FDA was 64.1% for large forms. A normalization module reduced ASR-related errors by 58%.
links.quote: While the code-switching module reduced ASR-related errors by 58%, failures occurred when phonetic noise was excessive.

links.outcome: Field detection accuracy of proposed pipeline versus rule-based and simulated commercial baselines
links.effect: Medium forms FDA: rule-based 76%, simulated Dragon 83%, proposed auto with annotations 94%, hybrid with annotations 98%. Large forms: 68%, 75%, 92%, 92% respectively.
links.quote: The proposed hybrid with metadata and normalization substantially outperformed both baselines, as detailed in Tables 6 and 7 .
